stem.en: A farmer's field loses a thin layer of topsoil every monsoon, and the crop gets a little smaller each year. There has been no flood or landslide. Which statement is correct?

text.en: No erosion is happening, because there has been no flood.

feedback.en: Erosion does not need a flood. Ordinary rain on bare ground can carry soil away.

text.en: This is weathering, because the rock is breaking down.

feedback.en: The soil is being carried away, so this is erosion, not weathering.

text.en: The subsoil is being lost, and crops grow in the subsoil.

feedback.en: It is the dark topsoil that is lost, and crops depend on it.

text.en: Erosion is happening, a little in each monsoon.

feedback.en: Right. Rain carries off a little soil each year, and yields fall.

explanation.en: Erosion can be slow. Rain running over the ground carries off a little topsoil each monsoon. Topsoil is the fertile layer, so yields fall even when no great flood has happened.

hints.en: Which layer is getting thinner, and where does it go?
